gap: No result ChatGPT got states surge watts per liter of enclosure. Measured that way, the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 leads with about 209 W/L (3,600 W ÷ 17.2 L), ahead of the DJI Power 1000 (190 W/L) and the OUPES Mega 1 (172 W/L), so ChatGPT's per-pound winner falls to third by bulk.
standout_why: I compared against Volt & Valley's best-of 2026 page (cited) and its high-surge page, plus Tested Watts' C1000 Gen 2 vs DELTA 3 Plus page (cited). Volt & Valley gives surge and weight (and dimensions for only a few units) but no per-liter figure, and says no maker in its registry publishes how long peak output is held. Tested Watts lists dimensions but computes no ratio. ChatGPT itself named 'surge watts per liter' as a metric but only filled in W/lb. The Enough Watts page that ChatGPT cited would not load (TLS error), so I could not check it. No rival notes that DJI publishes a 30-second overload rating, or that BLUETTI's '1,500W' for the Elite 30 V2 is Lifting Power, not surge.
decides: If 'for its size' means bulk, the pick changes: the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 gives the most surge per liter, and it is also the cheapest of the leaders at $499 on BLUETTI's US store today. If it means weight, the OUPES Mega 1 still leads (about 162 W/lb), with DJI second. The DJI Power 1000 is the only candidate whose maker states how long it holds an overload (2,600 W for 30 s on the 120 V DYM1000L model). That makes it the safest bet for hard motor starts. One caveat on the Elite 100 V2: its 3,600 W surge comes from a BLUETTI blog spec table, while BLUETTI's US product page advertises only '2,700W Lifting Power'.
